item.title: Pantograph 1.2.0
item.description:
New

  • Get Info (⌘I). See a photo's camera and exposure, and edit its title, caption, keywords, creator, copyright and date taken, or remove its location. The picture isn't re-encoded, so there's no loss of quality. For PDFs it edits the title, author, subject and keywords, and for any file it shows and edits Finder's Where From, the address it was downloaded from.
  • Straighten while cropping. A slider under the picture, or a two-finger turn on a trackpad, tilts the photo up to 45° either way while the crop stays level, so a crooked horizon can be squared up. It snaps back to level near zero.
  • Letter spacing in PDF text boxes. Tighten or loosen the letters in steps of 0.1 pt, or type a value, which helps line text up with the boxes on a form. Other PDF apps show it too.
  • Watermarks, and a command line for scripts and AI agents. The `pantograph` command (install it from Settings) watermarks images and PDFs with text or a logo, and converts, resizes, crops and straightens, adjusts, and edits information, all without opening a window. `pantograph mcp` offers the same tools to AI agents such as Claude Code; Settings copies the one-line setup.

If you have Pantograph 1.1.3 or later, it will offer this update by itself (1.1.7 and later install it quietly when you quit). Otherwise, download Pantograph-1.2.0.zip, unzip it and drag Pantograph to Applications. Requires macOS 13 or later; runs natively on Apple silicon and Intel. Signed and notarized by Apple.
